4000.title: Layer 3 objective exam outcome
4000.questionText: Entry from Layer 3 terminal nodes. Which objective examination outcome was reached? Management depends on this outcome together with the QuickDASH disability tier.

options.label: Primary adhesive capsulitis (Layer 3 node 3910)
Full-thickness rotator cuff tear (Layer 3 node 3920)
Partial rotator cuff tear or tendinopathy, or subacromial impingement (Layer 3 nodes 3930 and 3940)
Objective exam indeterminate (Layer 3 node 3950)

4100.title: QuickDASH functional severity (adhesive capsulitis)
4100.questionText: Administer the 11-item QuickDASH (each item scored 1 to 5, based on the last week). Score = ((sum of item responses / n) - 1) x 25, where n is the number of completed items. The score runs from 0 (no disability) to 100 (most severe disability) and cannot be calculated if more than 1 item is missing. What is the QuickDASH score?

options.label: Tier 1, low disability: QuickDASH less than 20
Tier 2, moderate disability: QuickDASH 20 to 50
Tier 3, high disability: QuickDASH greater than 50

4110.title: Adhesive capsulitis: disease stage and course of conservative care
4110.questionText: Primary adhesive capsulitis is managed nonoperatively first. Physical therapy is central across all disease stages, and physical therapy with a home exercise program is most useful early (freezing phase, pain predominant). Surgery is typically reserved for persistent symptoms after 6 to 12 months of conservative management. Where is the patient on this course?

options.label: Early disease (freezing phase) or less than 6 months of conservative care
Symptoms persist after 6 months or more of conservative care

4210.title: Rotator cuff tendinopathy: response to nonsurgical care
4210.questionText: Rotator cuff tendinopathy is managed with nonsurgical care and active rehabilitation. Adults with severe and persistent pain and/or disability despite a maximum of 12 weeks of appropriate nonsurgical care should be referred to a musculoskeletal physician specialist. How has the patient responded?

options.label: Less than 12 weeks of nonsurgical care, or improving
Severe and persistent pain and/or disability despite 12 weeks of appropriate nonsurgical care

4400.title: QuickDASH functional severity (full-thickness rotator cuff tear)
4400.questionText: Administer the 11-item QuickDASH (each item scored 1 to 5, based on the last week) to record baseline functional severity. Score = ((sum of item responses / n) - 1) x 25, where n is the number of completed items. The score runs from 0 (no disability) to 100 (most severe disability) and cannot be calculated if more than 1 item is missing. A full-thickness tear routes to orthopedic evaluation in every tier. What is the QuickDASH score?

options.label: Tier 1, low disability: QuickDASH less than 20
Tier 2, moderate disability: QuickDASH 20 to 50
Tier 3, high disability: QuickDASH greater than 50

4810.title: Structured physical therapy: adhesive capsulitis
4810.primaryDiagnosis: Conservative management of primary adhesive capsulitis with low to moderate disability: structured physical therapy (patient education, joint mobilization and manual therapy with ROM exercises, graduated home exercise program including self-stretching), with oral NSAIDs for symptom relief at clinician judgment. Avoid forceful or pain-provocative stretching. Reassess; escalate to orthopedic referral if symptoms persist after 6 months or more of conservative care.
differentials: Orthopedic specialist referral if persistent after 6 to 12 months

4820.title: Structured physical therapy: rotator cuff tendinopathy or impingement
4820.primaryDiagnosis: Conservative management of rotator cuff tendinopathy or subacromial impingement with low to moderate disability: structured physical therapy with progressive exercise therapy and a home exercise program, patient education and activity modification, with short-term acetaminophen or NSAIDs for pain. Reassess within a maximum of 12 weeks.
differentials: Orthopedic specialist referral if severe and persistent after 12 weeks

4830.title: Conservative care: indeterminate objective exam
4830.primaryDiagnosis: Conservative management with low to moderate disability and an indeterminate objective exam: physical therapy, short-term NSAIDs, and a home exercise program, with reassessment of the working diagnosis. Refer to an orthopedic specialist if severe and persistent pain or disability remains after 12 weeks of appropriate nonsurgical care.
differentials: Referred pain from the cervical spine

4910.title: Orthopedic evaluation: full-thickness rotator cuff tear
4910.primaryDiagnosis: Orthopedic specialist evaluation for a full-thickness rotator cuff tear. Physical therapy and operative treatment both improve patient-reported outcomes for small to medium symptomatic tears, but tear size, muscle atrophy, and fatty infiltration may progress over 5 to 10 years with nonoperative management, and healed repairs show better outcomes than physical therapy.

4920.title: Orthopedic specialist referral
4920.primaryDiagnosis: Referral to an orthopedic specialist (or other musculoskeletal physician specialist) for further assessment and treatment. Triggers: high disability (QuickDASH greater than 50), or persistent symptoms despite conservative care (more than 6 months in adhesive capsulitis; severe and persistent pain or disability after 12 weeks in rotator cuff tendinopathy).
